chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man, is it permissible for him to marry a woman with whom he had been immoral? He said: If he discerns maturity/reason from her, then yes; and if not, let him entice her to the forbidden (sexual act); if she follows him (to the forbidden act), then she is forbidden to him; and if she refuses, then let him marry her.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying a woman one has had illicit relations with according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides a nuanced juristic ruling for a man marrying a woman with whom he previously committed fornication, emphasizing the assessment of her moral maturity (*rushd*). The Imam outlines a practical test: if she consents to repeating the act, she becomes forbidden to him, whereas if she refuses, the marriage is permissible, highlighting the importance of her individual disposition in determining the validity of the union. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that prior fornication does not inherently invalidate marriage, provided the woman is deemed chaste or becomes so.
